title: Degree weight as a sum of squared coefficients
statement: Let $\Omega$ and $\iota$ be finite nonempty sets, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, and let $(\psi_a)_{a\in\iota}$ be a basis of real-valued functions on $\Omega$ that contains the constant-one function and is orthonormal for the $\pi$-weighted inner product. For any $n,k\in\mathbb N$ and function $f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$, the squared norm of the sum of Fourier components supported on coordinate sets of size $k$ equals the sum of the squares of the Fourier coefficients indexed by multi-indices with exactly $k$ nonconstant coordinates.
hypotheses_covered: Basis is orthonormal for the $\pi$-weighted inner product
